metas.name: Agriculture - Assam - Corn
metas.note: Within Assam, you can find corn between Guwahati and Nagaon, south of the river.
metas.footer: Source: BZH on GeoGuessr India

metas.name: Agriculture - Assam - Sugarcane
metas.note: Within Assam, sugarcane is mainly found around Lanka
metas.footer: Source: BZH on GeoGuessr India

metas.name: Agriculture - Bihar - Tea
metas.note: Within Bihar, tea plantations can be found in the far Northeast.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Canola
metas.note: Canola is mostly found in and around Rajasthan.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Agriculture - Cotton
metas.note: Cotton is commonly found in the western parts of India, particularly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Agriculture - Grape
metas.note: Maharashtra is by far the state with the highest grape production in India.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Madhya Pradesh - Sugarcane
metas.note: Within Madhya Pradesh, sugar cane can commonly be found southwest and northeast of the Satpura National Park.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Maharashtra - Cotton
metas.note:
Cotton (within) is mostly found around Nanded, more generally in the middle/eastern part of Maharashtra.

Note by MB: Very unreliable in my experience
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Maharashtra - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane in Maharashtra is mostly central from what I saw.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Oil Palm
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are almost exclusive to Andhra Pradesh and are mostly located around Eluru.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Pineapple
metas.note: Pineapple is very uncommon in India, but if you see it, it's in Bihar in the corridor between Nepal and Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane is most commonly found in the north in and around Uttar Pradesh, and in the southwest.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane - Tamil Nadu
metas.note:
Sugar cane can be found in several areas, the two main ones being near Erode and Thiruvanamalai.

It is also findable in smaller areas between those two big areas, but it is still mainly a northern Tamil Nadu thing.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Tea - Assam
metas.note: Within Assam, Tea is mostly planted in the eastern and in the southern regions. There are also some patches in Western Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Agriculture - Tea - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Tea plantations in India are mostly located in the northeast and in Kerala, but it spills in one particular area in Tamil Nadu northwest of Coimbatore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Agriculture - Tea - Tripura
metas.note: Within Tripura, Tea is found along the Bangladeshi border, and along the Assamese border.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Agriculture - Tea - West Bengal
metas.note: Within West Bengal, tea plantations are found near the northern border to Bhutan.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Agriculture - Tea Plantation
metas.note:
Tea plantations can be found in the northeast and the far south.

NOTE: If you find tea plantations in a flat area, you are likely in Assam or northeastern West Bengal, near the Assam border.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Agriculture - Telangana - Cotton
metas.note:
Cotton fields in Telangana are logically next to the big area that produces the most of it in Maharashtra, so it is gonna be found mostly north-west of the state. You can click in Nizamabad for a good score.

Note by MB: In my experience, it's more common North of Nizamabad.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Andhra Pradesh - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
Within Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs can commonly be found in three places.

  • Mainly south east of Guntur
  • Secondarily south of Nellore, where a rare red car can be found.
  • Sparsely around Srikakulam
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Assam - Thatched Roofs
metas.note: Within Assam, you can find thatched roofs all the way north east in the state.
metas.footer: Source: BZH on GeoGuessr India

metas.name: Architecture - Assam - Woven Walls
metas.note: In Assam, you can find houses with woven walls along the border to Arunachal Pradesh, north of Tinsukia.
metas.footer: Source: BZH on GeoGuessr India

metas.name: Architecture - Bihar - Tin Hip Roof
metas.note: If you see these hip roofs made out of tin - which are usually found in West Bengal - in Bihar, you're in the Northeastern Quarter of Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Bihar - Wide W Tiles
metas.note:
Within Bihar, you can find regular Wide W Tiles around Katihar.

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Blue Walls & Tiles
metas.note: Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a little less in Madhya Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Brick Kiln
metas.note: In poorer parts of the Ganges Valley it is common for villages to construct their own large chimneys to fire clay into bricks. These can be seen from far away and are a good clue for the Ganges Valley specifically, especially UP and Bihar. Note that they are also fairly common in the poorer eastern parts of Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Clay House
metas.note: Houses made out of clay are most common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. There's some spill in far southwestern Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Clay House
metas.note: Clay houses exist a lot in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and some spill can be seen in southwestern Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Clay Huts
metas.note: White painted clay huts are found in northwestern Bihar, northwest of Muzaffapur.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Colorful Walls
metas.note: Houses with colorful, particularly blue painted walls, can be found in the areas around Eastern Madhya, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Architecture - Corrugated Hip Roof
metas.note: Large hip roofs made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - Dravidian Temple
metas.note:
- Shorter and "pyramidal" towers (Vimana) - most easily recognizable

  • Monumental and ornate gate (Gopuram)
  • Door Guardian Statues (Dvarapala)

Found in the South of India.
metas.footer: Source: Wikipedia

metas.name: Architecture - Dumka House
metas.note: Houses between Dumka and Pakur have long tiled roofs and walls are painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Elevated Bengali Roof
metas.note:
Found mostly in the main, southern part of West Bengal, but more in the west. Sometimes also found in Bihar at the border to eastern Nepal.

Note by MB: This meta is not sufficiently researched, but it's still good to know
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Flat Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.note: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.note:
It has a “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Green House
metas.note: Houses in Odisha are often painted green.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Hay Hut
metas.note: These huts that are made entirely out of hay, and have thatched roofs are found in Southwestern Bihar, mainly between Patna and Gaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Jammu Architecture
metas.note:
Jammu looks like a fairly developed state compared to most places in India. The architecture looks richer and overall way nicer. Punjab has a similar architecture.

50/50 Tip ! It can be hard to differentiate Punjab and Jammu in urban rounds due to the similarity of their architecture. If you see rich looking houses, look at the car to know whether you are in Punjab or in Jammu. If you don’t see one of the two Jammu cars (boxy with top right thread or central strap, see image 3&4), click Punjab.

Note by MB: This 50/50 tip is not 100% reliable, so look at other clues (like Punjabi language) too.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Jharkhand - Wide W Tiles
metas.note: In the eastern parts of Jharkhand, you can find some West Bengal wide W tiles spill
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Flat Tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles can be spotted in random places in Madhya Pradesh, but mainly around Guna, Chhatarpur and Sagar in the center of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Slate Roofs
metas.note: Slate roofs in Madhya Pradesh can be found west of Sagar
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - U Tiles
metas.note: U tiles are more common in the eastern half of Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - W Tiles
metas.note: W tiles are quite rare in Madhya Pradesh but can still be seen west of Jabalpur and south of Guna
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Nalukettu
metas.note: Nallukettu architecture has distinct roofs, which are often very high and red. This style is often found around Kerala Backwaters.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Architecture - Odisha - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
Thatched roofs can be found pretty much all over the eastern coast of India. In the state of Odisha, they can mostly be seen between Balasore and Puri, but also more inland and in the southwest of the state.

If you see only thatched, the coast is more likely.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles
metas.note: U tiles are commonly found on the northwest of the state, on the borders with Jharkhand and Chhattsgarh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.note: When mixed with thatched roofs, U Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles
metas.note:
W tiled roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

  • corridor north of Bhubaneswar
  • Southwestern Odisha, southwest of Bhawanipatna
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
W tiled roofs combined with Thatched Roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

  • corridor north of Bhubaneswar
  • Southwestern Odisha, southwest of Bhawanipatna

Note by MB: This is also true if you just see W-Tiles, without Thatched Roofs.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & U-Tiles
metas.note: When mixed with W-Tiles, U-Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Orange/Black Wide W Tiles
metas.note:
If you see orange/black wide W tiles, you're probably around Madhubani (BR).

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Plastered Woven Wall
metas.note: Woven walls, plastered with clay are found on the western half of the Bihar-Nepal border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note: While Red Brick can be found anywhere in India, there is a notable concentration in the Ganges River Valley, especially towards the West.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Architecture - Shimla Vibes
metas.note:
Shimla is definitely the place in the Himalayas with the biggest amount of bright green and bright red roofs (and architecture in general).

Note by MB: It also spams Himalayan Cedars.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Sikhism
metas.note: Gurdwaras, which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab. You can also sometimes recognise them by the Sikh Khanda symbol, which represents the religion.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - Sikkim Roof
metas.note: Roofs in Sikkim often have this short "curtain" hanging down on the side of the roof.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Architecture - Slate Roof - Karnataka/Telangana
metas.note:
Slate roofs can be found in a very specific area between Kalaburagi and Hyderabad in Telangana.

Note by MB: This is the same area where they use the thin grey stones (see thin grey stones meta), and thus you can often see them in combination
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Square Panel Houses
metas.note: Houses made of square panels separated by thin beams are found in Northeast India, mainly in Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - Stick Huts
metas.note: Wooden huts with sticks around can be found in the western half of Bihar, at a latitude between Patna and Muzaffarpur..
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Tamil Nadu Colors
metas.note: Houses with very "strong colors", such as dark yellow, pink, purple, are often found in Tamil Nadu, and sometimes in Kerala and Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: Architecture - Tamil Nadu House
metas.note:
In Tamil Nadu, you will often come across quite good looking houses, the most recognizable are the ones with W tiled roofs and blueish paint. The combination of the color and the tiles should be 95% Tamil Nadu, the remaining 5% being spill in bordering states.

W tiled roofs are pretty much everywhere but somewhat less common in the northeast and on the eastern coast, where U tiles can be found more commonly.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Thatched Hay Roofs
metas.note: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Uttar Pradesh to Odisha tend to be made of fine pieces of hay.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Thatched Palm Roofs
metas.note: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried palm fans.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - Thatched Roofs - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are more common south east of Thanjavur.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Thin Grey Stones
metas.note: The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. These grey bricks and similar coloured rocks are sometimes also seen in walls and scattered on the ground in stockyards.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - Triangle Metal Roofs
metas.note: Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.note:
These rounded tiles are found mostly in

  • Chhattisgarh
  • Jharkhand
  • Bihar
  • Eastern Madhya

You can also find them in

  • Eastern Gujarat
  • Eastern Tamil Nadu
  • North-Western Telangana
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - U-Tiles - Tamil Nadu
metas.note:
U tiled roofs are quite rare in Tamil Nadu, but if you come across such roofs, it should be in the northeast.

It is possible to find some further down near Thanjavur, but it will more likely come with the combination of thatched roofs.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - W-Tiles
metas.note: W-Tiles are mostly found on the western coast and in Tamil Nadu, but it also goes further inland in western Madhya Pradesh and in Telangana.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - W-Tiles - Karnataka
metas.note: If you come across a W tiled roof in Karnataka, you can basically go in the western/southwestern part
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - W-Tiles - Telangana
metas.note:
The only type of tile in Telangana is the W tile type.

As you can see, it doesn’t go in the south of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Wealthy & Modern Homes
metas.note: Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very wealthy and modern homes.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Architecture - West Bengal - Dumka House
metas.note: In West Bengal, houses with walls painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom, are usually found near the Jharkhand border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Architecture - Wide W-Tiles
metas.note:
This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesn’t go further north than Purnia, Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Camera Meta - High Quality Shitcam
metas.note: The coverage on road NH326 (labelled 326) west of Brahmapur in Odisha has a thin grey antenna. The images are generally very high-quality for shitcam, with an especially high quality near the Harabhangi Reservoir.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Car - Kuno National Park Car
metas.note: This car has a back curving bar, but is mostly blurred. It can be found east of Kuno National Park
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Andaman Car
metas.note: This is the most common, though not only car on Andaman.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - Back Antenna
metas.note: Within Arunachal Pradesh, a back antenna can be found around Chowkam and East of Namsai.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - White Car with Mirrors
metas.note: Within Arunachal Pradesh, a white car with mirrors can be found on the road west of Itanagar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Assam - Back Antenna
metas.note: If you see a back antenna in Assam, you're in the far east of the state.
metas.footer: Source: BZH on GeoGuessr India

metas.name: Car Meta - Black Car
metas.note: This is not something you will come across very often, but if you have a black car and don’t really know where to go/want to confirm your guess, black car is more common in Telangana/Andhra Pradesh, especially in Northern Telangana and Coastal AP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Black Goa Car
metas.note: This black car, uniquely characterized through the black bars on each the side, is only found in Goa.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Boxy Car
metas.note: Large visible, square shaped cars can be found in all states northwest of Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, except for Madhya Pradesh. It can also be found in and around Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Car Meta - Boxy Car - 5 Indents
metas.note: A boxy car with 5 indents can be found near the river mouth of the Subarnarekha river near the Odisha/WB border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Boxy Car - 6 Indents
metas.note: A boxy car with 6 indents is found near Malkangiri, Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Boxy Car - Karnataka
metas.note: Boxy car in Karnataka is only found in and around Bengaluru.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Boxy Car - Odisha
metas.note: A boxy car with an extra step at the front is found in Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Car Meta - Flower Car
metas.note: A car with flowers on the front can be found around Keonjhar, on the 49 and the 20.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Goa/Daman Car
metas.note: This car (note the antenna!) can be found in Goa, and in the Union Territory of Daman.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Haryal Car
metas.note: This car is unique to Haryal, PB. It looks similar to the boxy car, but with a rounded front.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Himachal Pradesh - Boxy Car
metas.note: Shimla is the only city in Himachal Pradesh to have a boxy car, which is this car with the top right corner visible with a thread (sometimes not visible).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Jammu/Kashmir Car
metas.note:
White car, box car with bars and the central strap leaning right.

It can be found mainly in Jammu/Kashmir but sometimes in Sultanpur, UP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Ladakh Car
metas.note: All roads in Ladakh have this white car with visible front.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Adidas Car
metas.note:
The "Adidas Car" is characterized by the black stripes on the white car front. Sometimes it has a visible side mirror. It also often has a visible bar at the back.

It is exclusive to the island of Amini
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Big Blur
metas.note: A big circular blur (either full blurred or transparently blurred) is very common in Retrocam. On Lakshadweep, however, it is only found on Andrott and Kalpeni (both also have a car that's unique for these islands respectively).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred Black Front
metas.note:
This car with the subtle black blur at the front is found in Kalpeni. The blur can be very subtle sometimes, and is confusable with the blurred white edges on Agatti.

Sometimes the same car has a slightly different blur, where the edges are exposed.

Kalpeni can also have a big circular blur, so don't rule out Kalpeni if you don't see this car.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred White Edges
metas.note: This car is mostly blurred and has subtle white edges at the front. It's found on the island of Agatti. Sometimes the edges are so subtle that you can overlook them and confuse it with the Kalpeni car (which has a subtle black blur)
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Exposed Black
metas.note: This car with an exposed black front is unique to Kiltan. Note that the front is always exposed on Kiltan, if it's blurred (even partly), it's not the Kiltan car.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Red Car
metas.note:
The red front blur can be found on Andrott. Sometimes, the same car has a bit different blur, where there's some exposed red visible.

Note that Andrott can also have the big circular blur where you see no car.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Car with Mirror
metas.note: This car is the most likely to encounter if you get Lakshadweep. It has a white front and always a bit of mirror visible on the left. Sometimes a part of the mirror is blurred, but you can always see at least a bit of it exposed. This car is so common because it's on the main island of Lakshadweep, Kavaratti.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Exposed Front
metas.note: This car with an exposed white front is found of Kadmat. This car can be confused with others: It's not the Kadmat car if it has a visible side mirror. It's also not the Kadmat car if the front is blurred.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Mechuka Car
metas.note: Mechuka features a unique car in Arunachal. It can be found in the valley and on the road leading to it from Along on the NH13.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Mizoram - Double Mirror Car
metas.note: In Mizoram, a grey car with double mirrors appears in the southernmost coverage, near the NH502.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Mizoram - Long Antenna
metas.note:
If you see a long antenna, combined with a black car front in Mizoram, you're on the NH6 north of Serkhan.

Keep in mind this car is not unique to Mizoram.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Mizoram - Stubby Antenna
metas.note: A car with a black front and a stubby antenna within Mizoram can be found on the roads west of Aizawi.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - NH179B Car
metas.note: This car has an antenna with some kind of a spring. It basically goes from Salem to Chennai.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Open Trunk
metas.note: In the eastern parts of Ajmer, RJ, you can sometimes see an open trunk in Smallcam. It can be found north of Shrinagar/west of Circular Rd.
metas.footer: Discovered by TheRealWoly, shared on GeoGuessr India Discord, extent researched by Major Bajor.

metas.name: Car Meta - Orange Flag Car
metas.note: A car with an orange flag can be found in the Jharkhand north-east panhandle.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Punjab - Black Boxy Car
metas.note: Within Punjab, the black boxy car can be found on the Pakistani border between Firozpur and Amritsar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Punjab - Dasuya Forest Car
metas.note: Within Punjab, this car is is unique to Dasuya Forest. Beware that this car is not unique to Punjab though.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Punjab - Red Boxy Car
metas.note: Within Punjab, the red boxy car can be found in Ludhiana, Chandigarh, and a bit north between them. The coverage forms a reverse 'v'.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Racecar
metas.note: This cool car with a spoiler at the back can be found in Max-North Andaman, near Daglipur.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Rewa Car
metas.note: This car has a back curving bar at the front and white bars on the side. It's found mostly around Rewa, but also around Raipura.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Roing Car
metas.note: Within Arunachal Pradesh, both this black and this red car are exclusively found in Roing. The black car appears mainly on the NH313 and east. The red car appears mainly west of the main road.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh; self-researched

metas.name: Car Meta - Satpura National Park Car
metas.note: This car has a back-curving bar and a singular black bar. It's found mainly east of Satpura National Park, and sometimes around Raipura.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Tezu-Lohitpur Road
metas.note: If you see this white, boxy-looking car in Arunachal Pradesh, you're on the road between Tezu and Lohitpur.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Western Meghalaya Antenna
metas.note: In the very far western part of the Meghalaya, on the roads north of Purakhasia, you can find a particular car with an antenna on the top left. It can be quite hard to see so be aware it exists so you know what to look for
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - White Goa Car with bar
metas.note: This white car, uniquely characterized through the bar on the side, which is black and grey, is only found in Goa.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Car Meta - Yellow Car
metas.note:
While the car is blurred most of the time, Sikkim features a noticeable car that gives the western part of Sikkim, starting at Rangpo.

It can have an antenna, be blurred, almost invisible, but as long as you see a yellow car, you know it’s here.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Andaman Vibes
metas.note:
Andaman Islands are remote Islands that have their own distinct vegetation. It is covered in areca palm forests and the roads are often very thin.

Andaman has been covered using a camera with maxed out saturation somehow. The result is these very bright/white colors.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Kerala Construction Meta
metas.note:
In 2025, a large part of the NH-66 in Kerala is under construction, making it very recognizable.

If you see a long, straight highway with construction in Smallcam, you're likely to be on the NH-66.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Tripura Cam
metas.note: Many locations in Tripura have a pretty low brightness, despite the sun being out and not setting.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Yawal Double Smudge
metas.note: This double smudge can be found in the central-northern parts of the Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India-Discord, shared by GabrielGeo.

metas.name: Infrastructure - ∀-Poletop
metas.note:
Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A (∀) slightly below the top of the pole.

94% Madhya Pradesh 2% Jharkhand 1% each: Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - <-Poletop
metas.note: Poles with two diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape are common in Meghalaya (75%) and Arunachal Pradesh (20%) and occasionally found in Assam (2%).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - 1 1/2 Trapezoids
metas.note: This pole configuraiton is mainly found in Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - ACC Cement
metas.note: Found everywhere except for North-East.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ambuja Cement
metas.note: Commonly found everywhere, except for North East. Within North-East, it is sometimes found in Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Andaman Black Sticker
metas.note:
These black paint can be circular or square, features 2 letters, an arrow beneath, and some numbers beneath that and can be on metal/concrete poles.

They're found mostly near the capital (Port Blair/Sri Vijaya Puram) (95%) and rarely near Diglipur (5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Andaman Horizontal Bar Poletop
metas.note: Pole tops in Andaman mostly consist of horizontal bars perpendicular to the pole. They are not 100% unique to Andaman, but are very common there.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Antioquia Pole
metas.note: This black-yellow-black pole painting (which is famous for appearing in Antioquia in Colo), can also be found in Eastern Bihar along the Ganges.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Black & White Bollard
metas.note:
These bollards are rarer and not unique to Arunachal Pradesh, but if you think you are here, these are the areas these bollards are most commonly found

  • In Max West Arunachal Pradesh
  • North of Deed
  • North of Aalo
  • on the 319 in the East
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Divided Road
metas.note: The only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh is the NH415 south of Itanagar
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Pole Band
metas.note: A section of the NH13 west of Roing has poles marked with white numbers on blue, red or black paint.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Assam / West Bengal vans
metas.note: These vans (can be white, red, or orange) with specifically yellow plates, in NE India are found only within West Bengal and Assam. Doesn’t count with a white plate.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Infrastructure - Assam Pavement
metas.note: Many roads in Assam are paved with these tiles. What makes it stand out is that it is also found on very rural roads.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Infrastructure - Assam Trident Poles
metas.note: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam (98%).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bangur Cement
metas.note:
Bangur Cement is found in large parts of India.

It is only sometimes found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi (where Bangur Power Cement) is more prevalent.

It is never found in

  • Kerala + Tamil Nadu
  • North East India
  • Gujarat
  • Anything North of Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bangur Power Cement
metas.note:
Found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes also in Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh.

Don't confuse this with Bangur Cement, which has a different distribution.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bar underneath Generic Pole
metas.note:
Metal crossbar with no insulators

Most common in Maharahstra (50%)

Also occasionally found in other northern states.

Within the Northeast, it's exclusive to Tripura.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Big Ring Pole
metas.note:
Big rectangular metal ring around the pole.

Most common in Uttarakhand + Himachal Pradesh and Mizoram + Tripura.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bihar Pole + Mountains
metas.note: In Uttarakhand, the Bihar pole (yellow and black stripes) can be found on the NH109 North and a small road South of Dwarahat. Since Uttarakhand is mountainous, you shouldn't mistake it for Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bihar stripes
metas.note: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bihar/Jharkhand Guy
metas.note:
In Bihar and Jharkhand you will see many ads with this man with a turban and a beard. He's usually accompanied by a hexagonal company logo and a yellow background.

Note by MB: This sounds ridiculous but he seems to be so popular that there are copycats of him with the same Turban/beard style. So if you see a different company logo, don't trust this.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Tuk-Tuks
metas.note: Black Tuk-Tuks are most common in Maharashtra (maybe fake meta)
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Infrastructure - Blue & White Bridge
metas.note: The bridges in West Bengal frequently feature blue and white concrete blocks. It is also rarely found in Bihar around the city of Gaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Blue Pole Stickers
metas.note: These blue stickers on metal poles can be found on the NH109 near Lohali (UK)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Buddhism
metas.note:
Buddhist prayer flags and other Buddhist signals are mostly found in the Himalayas. Sometimes you can also find them in the Northeast, around Bangladesh, especially in Western Meghalaya, Western Mizoram and Southern Tripura. Rarely you can find it in central-eastern Maharashtra around Nagpur.

Note by MB: The colors in the map don't exactly match the text. The text is right though (for Geoguessr), not the map.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Lampe Circles
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as round yellow markings on street lights.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Large Blue Signs
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as blue signs mentioning sectors and industrial areas.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Streetsign
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as street signs which will typically feature several numbers rather than street names.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chandigarh Poletop
metas.note:
Trident poletop, V-shaped bars underneath and Punjab Poletop.

Very hyperspecific for some roads in Chandigarh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chennai Wall
metas.note: This wall pattern can be found in and around Chennai (but it is rare).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chettinad Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the C-Logo Found in South India, and sometimes in Goa and Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Combination of Even and Uneven Poletop
metas.note: In the northeast you may find poles with a combination of an even and uneven poletop.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Complicated Dark Metal Pole
metas.note:
Overly complicated, usually dark metal.

90% in West Bengal.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Concrete Blocks
metas.note: Concrete blocks, similar to those you see in Bhutan, are commonly found in (but not limited to) North-East India
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: Infrastructure - Concrete Holey Poles
metas.note:
Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Gujarat uses a variety of poletops, some of which can be used to identify other states. Beware that holey poles generally take precedence over poletop metas.

NOTE: They are rarely found in other states:

  • Maharashtra (2%)
  • Madhya Pradesh (1%)
  • Chhattisgarh (1%)
  • Odisha (0.5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Concrete Road / Yellow Lines
metas.note: From the city of Sukma to the border with Andra Pradesh, the NH30 has yellow road lines and is made of concrete. (Kinda similar to the famous Ruta 9 in Chile)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Concreto Cement
metas.note: Found in East India (i.e. Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha)
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Dark Rock Walls
metas.note: Dark Rock Walls are commonly found around Udaipur, RJ.
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: Infrastructure - Dehradun Sticker
metas.note: These round white stickers can be found all over Dehradun (UK)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Delhi Bus
metas.note: Orange and bright green buses are typically found in Delhi.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Delhi stripes
metas.note:
Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.

#1 clue for rural Delhi (98%)

Has to be the exact order and color.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Delhi Yellow Sticker
metas.note: Besides Kerala and Uttarakhand, Delhi can also rarely have yellow stickers. All of these regions look very different.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Double Bull Cement
metas.note: Found in Central and East India, in Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Duraguard Cement
metas.note:
Found in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh, sometimes in Odisha.

Don't confuse with Duraton Cement.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Duraton Cement
metas.note:
Only found in Punjab and Jammu / Kashmir.

Don't confuse with Duraguard Cement.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Elevated Jharkhand Structures
metas.note: These elevated structures are found a lot of them between Hazaribagh and Ranchi in Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Elevated Railway
metas.note:
Elevated railways can be found in the following cities:

  • Bengaluru
  • Chennai
  • Delhi
  • Hyderabad
  • Jaipur
  • Kochi
  • Kolkata
  • Mumbai
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Extended Vertical Bar
metas.note:
Extra vertical bar at the top of the pole, extends significantly over the pole.

85% West Bengal 12% Chhattisgarh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Generic Poletop
metas.note: Typically not south of Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Odisha except in Kerala. Generic pole does NOT include any bars on the top of pole
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Generic Poletop with Grey Crossbar
metas.note:
If the generic poletop has a grey crossbar, you're most likely in Uttar Pradesh. It's less commonly found in Odisha, Bihar, and more rarely in Haryan and Jharkhand.

If it's in South India, it's 98% Kerala.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Goa Poletops
metas.note:
This poletop has two crossbars, the top one is short with 2 insulators, the bottom one is long with 4 insulators.

It's mostly found in Goa (95%) and rarely in Kerala (2%), Maharashtra (1%) and Karnataka (1%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Green Pole Stripes
metas.note: Green pole stripes are commonly found in the far western roads of Arunachal Pradesh. They are often combined with yellow or white stripes.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gujarat - Non-Holey Pole
metas.note: Almost all poles in Gujarat are holey poles. Generic poles are only found sometimes in very far west Gujarat, near the border with Pakistan
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Harsil Road
metas.note: On the road south of Harsil (UK), you will find a large amount of poles with red/yellow stripes and black bollards with stripes (see UK/JH bollard)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - HiBond Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the wavy triangle logo. Found only in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Himachal Pradesh - Double Guardrail
metas.note: The NH5 near Sarahan ist the only road in Himachal Pradesh with a double guardrail.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Hollow Metal Pole
metas.note:
This means, it has an indent that runs through the whole pole. If you look at it from the top, it looks like a C.

Most common in Mizoram, seen in Himachal Pradesh as well.

Note by MB: Seen this in central states too, but still useful together with landscape ig.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Hyderabad Mesh Pole
metas.note:
Mesh pole with three wires on one or both sides, that are connected to the pole in a "pyramid shaped" extension on the side.

Note that it has to be a pole, not a cellphone tower (which would be a lot larger).

Found around Hyderabad, TG
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - JK Lakshmi Cement
metas.note:
Found in North and Central India, plus Jharkhand, Odisha and Gujarat. Sometimes also in Maharashtra.

Don't confuse with JK Power Cement (which hasn't been researched yet).
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - JSW Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, Goa + Maharashtra, and Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole
metas.note:
In Karnataka (85%), and sometimes in Haryana (6%), Western Andhra Pradesh (6%) and rarely Uttar Pradesh (1%), you can find trident poletops on concrete poles where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There are different variants of this poletop that increase the likelihood for Karnataka.

Note by MB: Make sure not to confuse it with the trident with a small bar at the top (see images).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole - Karnataka Insulator
metas.note:
If a trident pole has these insulators with three circles and air between them, it is found 98% in Karnataka.

The other versions of this poletop have lower certainties for Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kerala "Weird" Poletop
metas.note: Made of metal, has a "generic" crossbar, but additionally a very long bar that extends into one direction at the top, which holds the actual insulators.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kerala Bollard
metas.note: What makes these bollards unique is the red reflector on a stone bollard.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kerala Bridge
metas.note: Blue and white bridges can commonly be found all over Kerala. They can sometimes be painted in green.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kerala Yellow Marker
metas.note:
Small yellow pole markings are commonly found in Kerala.

Can also be used to rule out Kerala since 80-90% of all poles have it.

Can also be found in Goa (2-3%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Konark Cement
metas.note: Found in Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Large Rectangle
metas.note: In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

AP stands for Andhra Pradesh.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Madhya Pradesh - Rock Walls
metas.note: In Madhya Pradesh, rock walls are very common around two national parks : Kuno National Park and Panna National Park
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Maharashtra Pole
metas.note:
This pole is either metal or concrete (but more skinny than a generic pole). It has one or two small bars near the poletop.

It's not exclusive to Maharashtra, but very common there.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Manipur Poletop
metas.note: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Max Cement
metas.note: Found only in North-East India, but not in Nagaland or Arunachal Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Meghalaya - Divided Road
metas.note:
The NH6 north of Shillong is the only divided highway in Meghalaya.

Note by MB: A good way to tell you're in Meghalaya is the lack of non-latin scripts.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Metal Holey Poles
metas.note: Metal holey poles are common in Kerala.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Metal Mesh Poles

metas.name: Infrastructure - NH51 / Gujarat

metas.footer: Source: bibberbang1234 on the LearnableMeta Discord + additional self research

metas.name: Infrastructure - Odisha Bridge
metas.note: Some bridges in Odisha are made of green and white concrete blocks as guardrails

metas.name: Infrastructure - Orange Pole Paint

metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: Infrastructure - Orange Pole Stickers

metas.name: Infrastructure - Painted Stripes

metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Pole with Black/White bottom
metas.note:
White and black stripes on the bottom of a pole are found in both Meghalaya and Tripura.

Note by MB: Don't confuse this with the Tamil Nadu polepainting, which is always white-black-white and further up on the pole.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Pole with Red Paint
metas.note:
Silver painted poles with a red or brown top.

Common in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Tripura & Mizoram.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Punjabi Electricity Counters
metas.note: Electricity counters in Punjab are usually mint green with small window-like squares. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Pure Metal in Uttarakhand
metas.note: In the Himalayas, pure metal poles are usually more common in the North-East. If you see them in the Northwest, it's most likely Uttarakhand.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.note: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling you’re in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rajasthan Mesh Pole
metas.note:
Found 90% in Rajasthan.

Sikkim and Telangana also have Mesh poles, but they're different.

The Sikkim pole is slimmer, while the Telangana pole has "triangles" at the top.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ramco Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, however less common in Karnataka. Sometimes also found in West Bengal.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Red & White Bollard
metas.note: It is quite rare to see red and white bollards, but they are mostly found in far west Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Red&White Tree Paint
metas.note: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rusted Hollow Pole
metas.note: Thin rusted Poles that are hollow, i.e. have an indent going from the bottom to the top, are found in Maharashtra, and sometimes in Chhattisgarh.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Sanghi Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the Lion Logo. Found only in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Seperated Bus Lane
metas.note: On large roads in Ahmedabad and Surat you can find separated middle lanes for buses. Beware that people will still often drive in these lanes.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Shree Cement
metas.note: Found everywhere, except for Himalayan states, North Eastern States, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.note: Taxis in Sikkim often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Simple Black Sticker
metas.note:
This black sticker usually just has few characters, often just a number.

35% Tamil Nadu 35% Andhra Pradesh 20% Telangana

Note that it's a weak meta for Andhra over Telangana.

Do not confuse for Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Small Extra Bar
metas.note:
Short bar at the top of the pole.

Mostly in Rajasthan and Telangana Sometimes Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra Rarely Jharkhand.

In the Northeast, it can be found in Tripura or rarely in Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Small Ring Pole
metas.note:
Very similar to a second vertical bar, but it is attached to the pole on its ends, rather than in the middle, giving it a ring shape. What differentiates it from the big ring pole is that the bar isn't far away from the pole.

35% Maharashtra 35% Madhya Pradesh 20% Chhattisgarh 2% Rajasthan & Mizoram 1% Tripura
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Small Trapezoid
metas.note:
Trapezoid poletop, but the diagonal bars do not reach the end of the crossbar.

Most common in flat Arunachal Pradesh Sometimes in Tripura
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Square Stick Fences
metas.note:
In the northeast you will commonly see fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern.

They can also sometimes be seen in Odisha, which has a very different landscape, making it useful to distinguish Odisha from other eastern states.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & self-researched

metas.name: Infrastructure - Star Cement
metas.note: Found in North-East India, West Bengal and sometimes Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.note:
60% Tamil Nadu 20% Telangana 15% Andhra Pradesh

metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - T-shaped Pole Extension
metas.note:
This pole extensions (above the pole) with 3 insulators

45% Andhra Pradesh 45% Telangana 9% Tamil Nadu

3 insulators in a horizontal line, or middle insulator slightly above others

metas.name: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole
metas.note: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Bars in different directions
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If the bars point in different directions, it's often in Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Dark Metal / Single Bar
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If it's a single bar, with dark metal, it's 80% Meghalaya 15% Assam
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Grey Metal
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If the pole is made out of bright/grey metal, it's 45% Meghalaya 45% Assam
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Poles - Dark Metal / Double Bar
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If it's dark metal and has two bars, it's 65% Meghalaya 15% Assam 15% Mizoram
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

97% Andhra Pradesh

If it's not made out of dark metal, it's less certain.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole (Concrete)
metas.note:
A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid.

80% Chhattisgarh 10% Maharashtra 3% Karnataka 2% Odisha 1% each: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam

NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present. Northeast India also has some trapezoid poletops that look a bit different.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop

Triangle poletops with three insulators on top can be found in Jammu and Kashmir, sometimes in Himachal Pradesh.

Found 98% in Karnataka 0.5% in Gujarat
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tripura Pole

metas.name: Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - High Bar

Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope

metas.name: Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - Low Bar

Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).

If it's lower on the pole (meaning you can see a bit of concrete over the bar), it's 85% Andhra Pradesh, 15% Telangana

Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - UK/JH Bollard

Found in Northern States: Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, sometimes Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

Note by MB: This only counts if it's black, not with other colors.

99.3% Tamil Nadu 0.02% Andhra Pradesh 0.01% Madhya Pradesh
