metas.name: Infrastructure - Windfarms
metas.note:
The places with the most wind farms are indeed Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. This is pretty advanced knowledge, but region guessing states can be possible by learning where wind farms are:

  • Gujarat: Southwestern half
  • Karnataka: Davanagere to Hubballi
  • Tamil Nadu: Max South; Around Coimbatore
  • Maharashtra: Tristate to Madhya and Gujarat; Around Jath (southern)
  • Rajasthan: Jodhpur to Jaisalmer
  • Madhya Pradesh: West & North of Indore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Window Poletop
metas.note: Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab and Haryana. 93% Punjab 4% Haryana 1% Delhi & Jammu (on Punjabi border) 0.5% Rajasthan 0.2% Ladakh
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Wonder Cement
metas.note: Found Northwest of Madhya Pradesh, however not in Himachal Pradesh or further North.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.note:
Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct yellow outer road lines and fresh dark pavement.

NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these lines exist in other states as well.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Bands
metas.note: Between Aizawl and Champhai on the NH6, poles will have yellow bands.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Stickers
metas.note: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Tuk Tuk / Black Roof
metas.note:
Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

NOTE: They can also rarely be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Zuari Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, especially in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: Infrasturcutre - Karnataka Symmetrical Poletop
metas.note:
2 insulators on each side, with the top of the pole sticking out.

Found in Karnataka (94%) and rarely in Tamil Nadu (4%) or Kerala (1%)
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: Landscape - Amygdaloidal Basalt
metas.note:
This is a volcanic rock, which is recognizable by it's dark color with white mineral patches on it.

It is mostly found between Pune and Jalgaon.

It's important to note that this rock alone, without the mineral patches is more widely spread.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on The Real Meta Research Group (RMRG) Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Andhra Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.note:
Andhra Pradesh has a long coast along the bay of Bengal and it is fairly recognizable because of the red soil combined with overall flatness. This is the area in which you fill find red soil in Andhra Pradesh.

Flat landscape with red soil and lots of Palmyra should pretty much always give the eastern India coast.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Anisun River Valley
metas.note: A rocky desert can be found in this valley southwest of Nandyala, AP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Assam - Hilliness
metas.note: Hilliness in Assam is found mostly South or East of Nagaon.
metas.footer: Self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Assam - North Mountains
metas.note: If you see Mountains to the North in Assam, you're on the border to Arunachal Pradesh. In my experience, this is a particularly common sight on the border east of Itanagar.
metas.footer: Self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Badvel Valley
metas.note:
Wind turbines aligned on top of mountain ranges are very common in these mountain ranges valleys I would say. (I know there are some in RJ as well)

Even without wind turbines, you can click in this valley if you have a good north/south angle. I would even say that it is the only place in India with such big N/S dry ranges to the west AND to the east.

Differentiations:

  • Western ghats mountains in Maharashtra (Pune-Nashik area) have different angles
  • The other Mountain Range in Andhra Pradesh (near Odisha border) is less dry.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Chaukhamba
metas.note: Chaukhamba, located near the town of Ukhimath, is a mountain massif covered in snow which can be recognised by its three distinct peaks, with the centre peak being the tallest.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
Coastal Andhra Pradesh is characterized by a flat, agricultural landscape with coastal bushes

50/50 Tip ! Similar bushes can also be found in Gujarat, but Gujarat will often have distinct holey poles or have a boxy car. Also, Gujarat will primarily have date palms whereas Andhra will have palmyra palms as the main occurrence in palm trees.

The harder rounds in Andhra are the coastal, agricultural ones without any Palmyra or any pole. This basically becomes a 50/50 with any other flat & agricultural state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Dark Soil
metas.note: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Dark Soil - Karnataka
metas.note:
Dark soil in India is usually found in and around Maharashtra.

In many cases you can see trident poles together with this dark soil, which will put you in Northern Karnataka, usually near the Maha border (free 4.5k+)
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Dry Ganges River Valley
metas.note: Southern Haryana and Southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural, but often still look dry. These areas look like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.note: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Dry TG/AP
metas.note: If you have a Telangana/Andra pole or Telugu with a dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur, AP and Shadnagar, TG (see image)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Elevated Dry Road
metas.note: Elevated Roads (similar to Bangladesh), with a dry landscape, are common in and around Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Landscape - Elevated Jammu & Kashmir
metas.note: While a lot of the coverage in Jammu is located in flat parts, there are some areas north and northeast of the city of Jammu with elevation, where you will be able to see a lot of pines.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Ganges River Valley
metas.note:
The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.

Note by MB: Agriculture can be found in many parts of India. I think what sets apart these Northern Plains is the lack of palm trees (except for the occasional date palms and the Palmyra palm spam in Bihar).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Gujarat - Dead Landscape
metas.note:
Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.

NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Guntur Landscape
metas.note:
Around Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, you can find a landscape that combines the Andhra Pradesh Panhandle and the agricultural east coast further south.

You will have lots of agriculture (more than in Panhandle) and also many palm trees (more than in the coastal region further south).
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Haryana - North Haryana vibes
metas.note:
The northern part of Haryana is very green and agricultural.

Note by MB: Ganges River Valley in general looks like this, but I feel like this area is even greener and lusher, and it also has more sugarcane.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Himachal Pradesh - North/South Valley
metas.note:
The city of Manali is fairly recognizable due to it being one of the two areas with coverage in a recognizable north-south valley. The other is from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south of it.

The only way I came up with to tell the 2 apart is the vegetation but this is kinda fake since both cities are located in the same valley.

According to me, Manali has poplar trees and pines within the city whereas the other area doesn’t have much of those and mostly consists of random trees.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Himalayas
metas.note: The by far tallest mountains in India are found in the Himalayas.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Ladakh - Snow Coverage
metas.note: Coverage extends to roads that are very high in altitude, so snow can be visible on the end of the streetview east of Leh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Madhya - Elevated
metas.note: There are a few places where you can have elevation in Madhya Pradesh. The main elevation areas are around Yawal and satpura park, as well as south of Indore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Madhya Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.note: Within Madhya Pradesh, a reddish or pinkish soil is generally more common towards the East.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched by Jayden and me

metas.name: Landscape - Maharashtra West Coast
metas.note: The landscape west of the Western Ghatts in Maharashtra is quite unique. It has a lot of forests, and a dark brown soil. It's mostly a vibe thing, but it looks kinda like Kerala but with less palms.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Mechuka Valley
metas.note: The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. North of Mechuka the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Meghalaya Hills
metas.note: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded, smooth hillsides with a flat top.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Mizoram Hills
metas.note: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Monoliths
metas.note: Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Mountains in Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Mountains in Tamil Nadu can be found along the western border. Additionally, there's a lot of mountains west of Madurai and some east of Salem.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
metas.note: This section of road features huge mountains, with a little bit more **green on their slopes. **
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Panhandle Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks quite different than the rest of the state. It is much greener (and has an arguably "darker greener" tone). There are also A LOT more coconut palms here than anywhere else in AP.

Other parts of Andhra Pradesh do have Palmyra Palms, but Coconut palms are kinda rare outside of the panhandle.

The area south of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh can also look extremely similar, but it has a lot less coverage.
metas.footer: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Punjab - Elevated
metas.note: Punjab is generally a very flat state. If you know you're in Punjab, but it's hilly or mountains, you're on the border to Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Rajasthan - Mountains
metas.note: The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar max northeast and Udaipur - Mount Abu area
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Rajasthan - NorthEast Ridge
metas.note: In Rajasthan, there is a North-east angled ridge going from Mount Abu area to New Delhi
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Rajasthan - Rolling Hills
metas.note: In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common for the area south of Udaipur
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Rajasthan Vibes
metas.note: Rajasthan is a state that is drier than its surrounding states. It's difficult to explain, but many locs in Rajasthan just have a certain 'drier' vibe. If you saw this loc and thought 'This looks like Rajasthan', pat yourself on the back :)
metas.footer: Self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Red soil
metas.note: Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Rewa Ridge
metas.note: A pretty straight east-west range with a slight north east angle can be found near Rewa. It is fairly easy to recognize.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Rockiness
metas.note:
Telangana and Andra Pradesh have a lot of “rockiness”. It can be rocks on the side of the road, boulders or even rocky hill slopes but they share that in common.

I found it to be more in Telangana so the meta is here, but note that it can extend to surrounding states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

Note by MB: In my experience, in AP, rockiness is very common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Rural Manipur Landscape
metas.note:
Since Imphal is located in a valley, it is fairly simple to recognize it after a few games.

The landscape around the city consists of agricultural fields surrounded by mountains, so it is pretty easy to know you are in Imphal.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Snow Coverage in the Mountains
metas.note:
This coverage can be found on the 3 in Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border.

The coverange extends from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai
metas.footer: Source: self-discovered

metas.name: Landscape - Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
metas.note: A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Spiti River Valley
metas.note:
The shape of the mountains iin this valley are truly unique : very dry, very high in elevation and sparsely green.

If you have trouble making the difference between this road and the NH3 to the west because it looks roughly similar, just know that the NH3 is paved whilst the Spiti river valley roads usually are not.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Tirupati
metas.note: The city of Tirupati, AP can easily be recognized by the huge ridge in the North. Other metas, like black&yellow Tuk-Tuks, two-indent poles or simply Telugu language, can help confirm.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Western Ganges River Valley
metas.note: The western Ganges River Valley (Punjab/Haryana/Western UP) usually looks wetter and greener than the general Ganges River Valley. You can often see rice and sugarcane. Note that areas like this can still be found in other parts of the river valley, this is not a 100% meta
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Western Ghats
metas.note:
The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Western Meghalaya Landscape
metas.note:
The western part of Meghalaya basically looks like bangladesh with hills. There are a lot of areca palms, banana trees and palms.

“Hilly forests with areca palms surrounding flat agricultural fields” is how I would best describe this part of Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Landscape - Western Rajasthan Landscape
metas.note: The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Western Uttarakhand Landscape
metas.note: The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Wonky Hills
metas.note: The Odisha Hills are very "wonky", i.e. they're undulating and can also very greatly in height.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Landscape - Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary
metas.note: Unique hilly landscape with dead trees. Note that not all coverage in this park looks like this.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Language - Assamese
metas.note: Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably ৰ and ৱ.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Bengali
metas.note:
Bengali is found in northeastern India and has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring left-facing triangular shapes.

NOTE: This is also the language found in Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Devanagari Script
metas.note:
Hindi is the most common language in India and can be found in many central and northern regions. It uses the Devanagari script, which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.

Note by MB: Maharashtra has a different language that uses the same script.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Gujarati
metas.note: Gujarati, found in Gujarat, has a script with several similarities to the Hindi script, however it notably lacks the horizontal line at the top of every word.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Kannada
metas.note: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. It is very similar to the Telugu script, with Telugu having one additional feature described in the next tip. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Malayalam
metas.note: The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Marathi
metas.note:
Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script, however it sometimes uses the letter ळ which is not found in Hindi.

Further differences, analyzed by MB:

  • Vowels with this symbol on top (ऍ) are exclusive to Marathi
  • Marathi uses Western Full Stops '.' , while Hindi uses Devanagari full stops '।'
  • This letter: ण is more common in Marathi (but not exclusive)
  • Marathi does NOT use those dots (nukta) on the bottom left of a character: ज़
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & self-researched

metas.name: Language - Meitei
metas.note: Manipuri, also called Meitei, is the official language of Manipur. It is written using the Meitei script, which can be recognised by its many vertical lines and right angles.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Mizo
metas.note: Mizo, found in Mizoram, is the language most commonly found on the Indian coverage other than English, which uses the Latin script.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Only English
metas.note: The state of Meghalaya uses English primarily and no other scripts. Thus if you see a lot of signs and no non-english language, you are most likely in Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Language - Oriya
metas.note: The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles a skull emoji .
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Punjabi
metas.note: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters ਨ, ਲ and ਅ as well as a diacritic in the shape of a soft curve beneath a letter.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Tamil
metas.note:
The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.

NOTE: Tamil is also commonly found in Sri Lanka.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Language - Telugu
metas.note: Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, has a script very similar to Kannada, but you’ll often see diacritics resembling checkmarks at the top of letters.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Misc - AGP
metas.note:
The AGP's flag is an elephant on the dutch flag.

It operates only in Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - BGPM
metas.note:
Yellow - Grey - Dark Red Flag with a nice landscape in the middle and some Devanagari (!) text at the top.

Found in West Bengal near the Sikkim border.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - BJP
metas.note:
BJP is one of the most popular national parties in India. You can find its flags basically everywhere. However, they are less popular in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, meaning their flags are rare there.

Their symbol is a lotus flower.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - BJP Spam
metas.note:
The BJP is a popular national party, and thus it's flags can be found everywhere. Their symbol is a lotus flower.

It is most popular in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, so if you see a lot of BJP flags in one pano, you are likely to be in this belt.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Black & Yellow Taxis
metas.note: Black Taxis with yellow roofs are found in Meghalaya and Mumbai.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Misc - Bodoland People's Front
metas.note: This flag with this tool on an Indian background is found in Bodoland, which consists of the districts in Assam bordering Bhutan.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Communism
metas.note:
Communist symbolism is mostly found in Kerala. Second mostly, but significantly less, it's found in Tamil Nadu. Sometimes, it's also found in Tripura, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. You can rarely spot it in Maharashtra, West Bengal, Assam and Manipur.

The communist party has a youth organisation, the DYFI, with the same distribution.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - DMK
metas.note: Black and red colored flag. Other objects in this colors are also commonly found in the state of Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Donyi Polo
metas.note: This flag that resembles the Japanese flag stands for Donyi Polo, a religion found in Arunachal Pradesh between Ziro and Anini.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Gandhi Topi
metas.note:
This hat is called the Gandhi Topi is almost unique to Maharashtra. Note the shape which resembles a boat.

Note by MB: White hats in general are a common attire for Muslims in India, so make sure it's the boat shape.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on the GeoGuessr India discord

metas.name: Misc - Gorkha Seperatist Flag
metas.note: The flag is green-white-yellow and can be found in West Bengal near the Sikkim Border.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - IELTS
metas.note:
Advertisements for IELTS-exams are relatively often seen between Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh

Note by MB: Of course, advertisements like this can theoretically be found everywhere.
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: Misc - INC
metas.note:
INC is a popular national party, and found almost everywhere. The notable exceptions are West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, where the INC has regional versions, meaning you won't find any INC imagery there.

Their symbol is a flat hand facing you, on the background of the Indian tricolor.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - India Union Muslim League
metas.note:
Green flag with half moon and star, pointing at the top left corner.

This party is almost exclusively active in Kerala. Mostly in the districts of Kozhikode and Malappuram.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Jainism
metas.note: Jainism is a pretty rare minority religion. Jainist symbols are found mostly in Maharashtra, then Gujarat and Rajasthan, then Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Janata Dal
metas.note:
Flag is green-white-green, the symbol is an arrow.

Found only in Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Karbi Colors
metas.note:
The Karbi are an ethnic group that inhabit two districts in Assam, Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong.

Their flag is rarely shown, but you can often find Karbi colors (dark red, black and white) in those districts.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Karnataka Flag
metas.note: This is an unofficial flag of Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Kongunadu Makkal Desia Katchi
metas.note: Flag of a political party active only in Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Lungi
metas.note: People wearing a Lungi, which looks like a towel wrapped around the waist, are more common in South India.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on the GeoGuessr India discord

metas.name: Misc - Manithaneya Makkal Katchi
metas.note: Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Meitei Flag
metas.note: The Meitei people inhabit Manipur state, especially Imphal. Their flag is commonly found in and around that city.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Naam Tamilar Katchi
metas.note:
Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.

The tiger symbol can sometimes be found without the flag.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Navayana Buddhism
metas.note: This blue flag with this symbol in the middle is specific for Navayana Buddhism, the branch of Buddhism common in Central-Eastern Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Odisha Shell (Political Party)
metas.note: This shell is the symbol of a Odisha specific political party: Biju Janata Dal
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Misc - Samajwadi Party
metas.note: Exclusive to Uttar Pradesh, their symbol is a bicycle.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Sarnaism
metas.note: This flag and this symbol stand for Sarnaism. They are very localized, found in Ranchi and in Southern Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Scarfs
metas.note: People wearing colorful scarfs are generally found in the north of India.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Misc - Shivaji
metas.note: Shivaji is a person often depicted on statues in Maharashtra. He is always riding a horse, and is often accompanied by an orange flag.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Misc - SKM
metas.note: This party has an orange-red-green flag and a table lamp as a symbol. It operates exclusively in Sikkim.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Trinamool Congress / CMT
metas.note:
The flag of this party often has these flowers on some grass with the Indian flag as background.

It can be found mainly in West Bengal, however less commonly in the Northern Parts. Sometimes it's also found in Western Meghalaya
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - Tripra Mothi
metas.note:
Tripra Mothi is a Tripura-specific party. Its flag has two vertical stripes, yellow and red.

Don't confuse it with the Karnataka flag, where the stripes are horizontal.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - UPPL
metas.note:
The flag of UPPL is yellow white green with a farmer on a tractor on it. Found in Bodoland, which consists of the Assamese districts bordering Bhutan.

Don't confuse this with the Gorkha seperatist flag, which is green-white-yellow.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - VCK
metas.note: Blue and red flag with a Myanmar-style star, found only in Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Misc - YSR Congress
metas.note: This party is exclusive to Andhra Pradesh, and most popular in the South. Their symbol is a ceiling fan.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: Vegetation - Agave
metas.note:
Agaves are mostly found in Karnataka

Note by MB: This is generally a fake meta, Agaves can be found in many different places throughout India. But if you have really nothing else to go off, Karnataka is definitely a place to conside.r
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Vegetation - Areca Palm
metas.note:
Areca Palms can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown.

They are most common in Assam, but also in other northeastern areas, stretiching to coastal Odisha. A second common region is Kerala and coastal Karnataka
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Palms by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Assam - White Flowers
metas.note: In Assam, these white flowers can often be seen along the road in three areas: - The border to West Bengal - The border to Eastern Bhutan - West of Nagaon.
metas.footer: Source: BZH on GeoGuessr India

metas.name: Vegetation - Bhutan Cypress
metas.note:
Recognition (most visible when you look at the bottom of the crown):

  • symmetrical pattern of needles on twigs
  • thin twigs
  • twigs draping down

Found in:

  • mostly Western Sikkim and Sangti, Manda La, Salari (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • often in Khellong, Rupa (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • sometimes Rest of Sikkim, and Arunachal, west of Jamiri
  • rarely in West Bengal near Sikkim Border.
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Bhutan White Pine
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • whiteish-greyish tinge
  • Short needles
  • long slender cones
  • two rows of hanging needles
  • many branches, little space between them

Found in:

  • Max West Arunachal, Mechuka
  • sometimes Ziro, Neora Valley National Park (West Bengal)
  • very rarely Sikkim
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Blue Pine
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • individual branches well visible
  • edges of branches have thin brush of new needles
  • in higher elevation, the crown will be conical
  • needles drape down in all directions

Found in:

  • mostly: Max West Arunachal; Road south of Harsil
  • sometimes: Dharamshala, Manali, Kullu, Shimla, Sarahan, Southern Uttarakhand Mountains
  • rarely: Further inside the Uttarakhand mountains
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Calotropis Procera
metas.note: Calotropis Procera is found all over Rajasthan and less in surrounding states so it is a good clue for Rajasthan if you have a lot of it.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Vegetation - Chir Pines
metas.note:
Recognition

  • round crown
  • young pines: conical crown, thick brush for new needles Found in
  • Mountainous Uttarakhand; Shimla, Dalhousie (Himachal Pradesh); Elevated Jammu / Kashmir
  • Sometimes Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh)
  • Rarely low elevation dry valleys in Western Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Coconut Palms
metas.note: Coconut palms are most common in Kerala, the Western Half of Karnataka and Southern Coastal Maharashtra In general, they appear near Coasts, near the border to Bangladesh, and anywhere South of Central Telangana
metas.footer: Source: India Palms by duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Combination of Date Palm & Palmyra Palm
metas.note: In Jharkhand, you will very often see the combination of date palms (a lot of them) and palmyra palms. I think it is one of the best clues for getting Jharkhand because it’s pretty unique. I also saw a lot of that combination of palms in Telangana so be careful and look for text before guessing.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Vegetation - Date Palm
metas.note: Date palms can be found in Central India. They appear North of the Latitude of Chhattisgarh, except for Himalayan states, the Northeast and Western Gujarat/RJ.
metas.footer: Source: India Palms by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Date Palm - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Within Tamil Nadu, date palms can be found in the North-East.
metas.footer: Source: India Palms by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Dead Trees
metas.note: These 'dead'-looking trees are a very strong point to go to Rajasthan. They are concentrated mostly southwest of Sikar.
metas.footer: Research by prizrak and Unassumed, shared on GeoGuessr India Discord

metas.name: Vegetation - Doum Palm
metas.note: Doum palms, which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with multiple branches, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Vegetation - Eucalyptus
metas.note: Eucalyptus trees are a good clue for the Uttarakhand foothills and nearby areas in Uttar Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia
metas.note: This type of cacti (Euphorbia neriifolia) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia (Hilly Landcape)
metas.note: South of Udaipur, you can find a very distinct landscape with narrow hills and a lot of this type of cactus (Euphorbia).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Vegetation - Himalayan Cedar
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • downward bending branches
  • very short needles

Found in

  • Shimla, Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Palampur, Kasol, Jibhi, South of Kullu, South of Manali (HP); Road from Harsil to Gangotri (UK) and Southwestern UK in general
  • sometimes in Kangra, Solan, Manali-Dalang road (HP) and around Rudrapayag (UK)
  • rarely in eastern Uttarakhand
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Himalayan Hemlock
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • twig with two symmetrical rows of short needles
  • downward bending twigs
  • crowns look a bit disorganized

Found in:

  • South of Senge and South of Dirang (Western Arunachal Pradesh)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Indian Pitcher Plant
metas.note: The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of Umlārem.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt (lowkey useless)

metas.name: Vegetation - Jand Tree
metas.note:
This tree, often called Jand by Indians, can be recognized by the clusters of leaves at the end of thick branches.

It is found in Northern Rajasthan and Southern Haryana/Punjab.
metas.footer: Source: Jayden

metas.name: Vegetation - Japanese Cedar
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • puffy, conical crown
  • smooth reddish bark with parallel vertical indents
  • "sea grass twigs" (look at picture #3)
  • twigs growing in all directions

Found in:

  • Sikkim/WB Border
  • Meghalaya Hills
  • Dirang, Khellong, Bomdila (Arunachal)
  • sometimes more north in Sikkim and west of Jamiri (Arunachal)
  • rarely east of Jamiri (AR)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Khasi Pines
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • disorganized crowns, neither conical nor round
  • younger pines can appear round, but have shorter needles

Found in:

  • Meghalaya Hills
  • Raga & South of Ziro Junction (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • Imphal (Manipur)
  • Champhai, Darlawn (Mizoram) Less commonly:
  • Road from Ziro to Raga
  • North Vanlaiphai (Mizoram) Rarely:
  • Rest of Meghalaya and Mizoram
  • Arunachal Pradesh / Nagaland border
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Macaranga Peltata
metas.note: Parasol leaf tree (Macaranga peltata) is common along the southwestern coast anywhere south of Mumbai and seems to be virtually exclusive to that area, I have yet to find it anywhere else in India. To identify it, look for the teardrop shape of the leaves and the spot where the leaf stem connects to the inner part of the leaf blade.
metas.footer: Posted on Plantcord(Invite) by Avetixz

metas.name: Vegetation - Morinda Spruce
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • Dense Foliage
  • Shoots drape downwards

Found in:

  • Shimla, Kullu, Manali (Himachal Pradesh)
  • Uttarkashi, Dehradun, Ukhimath (Uttarakhand)
  • to a lesser extent: general area between Dehradun and Ukhimath
  • rarely in Eastern Uttarakhand
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Palmyra Palms
metas.note:
Palmyra Palms have a round crown with fan shaped leaves and a trunk with consistent thickness, giving them a lollipop shape.

They appear mostly in 3 areas:

  • Central Bihar
  • Coastal Pondicherry towards Andhra Pradesh/Odisha border + Telangana
  • Around Mumbai

They are also common in

  • coastal states from Tamil Nadu to West Bengal
  • Bihar & Eastern UP
  • Telangana
  • Eastern Gujarat
metas.footer: Source: India Palms by duskron

metas.name: Vegetation - Pindrow
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • Symmetrical Branches
  • Layered Clusters
  • Clusters shaped like an "inverse function" (see images)
  • narrow, conical, dense foliage

Found in:

  • Jibhi (HP), Chinyalisour, Ukhimath (UK)
  • sometimes Shimla (HP), Range from Dehradun to Rishikesh (UK)
  • rarely remaining UK Mountains; Dharamshala, Palampur, Kullu, Kasol, Manali (HP)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.note: West of Mount Abu, you can find a lot of Euphorbia cacti with flat landscape. Note that this meta is only specific for Rajasthan, Euphorbia appears in other states, like Gujarat, too.

metas.note:
Recognition:

  • Symmetrical Shoots
  • Longer Needles
  • Small shoots make triangular shape
  • Seperated clusteres at different hights

Found in

  • Senge, Manda La (AR)

metas.name: Vegetation - Sikkim Larch
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • no needles in winter (which is currently all coverage in India with this tree)
  • Conical structure that resembles a christmas tree
  • lighter needles (if present)

Found in:

  • around Senge
  • sometimes around Manda La (both Arunachal Pradesh)

metas.name: Vegetation - Sikkim Spruce
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • needles organized in seperated clumps
  • darker than pines
  • individual branches visible (on high trees)
  • new shoots & many buds often visible from afar
  • Unique branch structure

Extremely rare in India, so far only a singular tree has been found in Manda La.

metas.note: Teak forests in wet season with boxy car can be found around the Gujarat-Maharashtra border between Surat and Nashik. The trees are quite distinctive, tall and narrow.
